html:
The Shíshálh, or Sechelt, are a Coast Salish First Nation of the Sunshine Coast of British Columbia, from Roberts Creek north to Jervis Inlet. They speak Sháshíshálhem, a Salishan language.

They lived in winter villages on the inlets and fished, gathered shellfish and hunted. Catholic missionaries had strong influence among them from the 1860s. In 1986 the Sechelt Indian Band Self-Government Act made them the first First Nation in Canada to govern itself outside the Indian Act. Their neighbours include the Squamish and the Tla'amin. See also Coast Salish.
